body.p: After you install the Git Client add-on, a top-level Git menu is available in the main menu bar. Use this menu as a repository-level entry point for common Git actions.

Most actions from the Git menu apply to the current working copy selected in the Git Staging view. If an action needs a Git repository and no working copy is selected, the Git Client prompts you to select or create one when possible.

section.title: Menu Groups
section.p: The Git menu is organized around the following groups of actions:

dlentry.dd: Clone a repository, open an existing repository, create a repository in the project, or open the working copy folder in the system file manager or a terminal window.
Push local commits to the remote repository or pull remote changes into the local repository.
Open the Git Client views, inspect branches, show tags, show history, or work with submodules when the repository contains them.
Save local changes in a stash or open the list of existing stashes.
Manage remote repositories, track a remote branch, edit the repository configuration file, or open Git Client settings.
Clones a remote repository into a new local folder.
Selects an existing local Git repository as the current working copy.
Creates a repository in the project folder. This action is enabled when a Git repository does not already exist there.
Opens a submenu for opening the current working copy folder in the system file manager or in a terminal window.
Pushes your local repository changes to the remote repository.
Opens a submenu for pulling changes from the remote repository. The submenu includes pull actions for merge, rebase, or pulling from a remote branch other than the one being tracked.
Opens the Git Staging view.
Opens the Git Branch Manager view.
Opens a dialog box that lists all tags. You can delete tags, checkout a specific tag, or push a tag that is only present in the local branch to the remote repository.
Opens the Git History view.
Opens a submenu where you can select a submodule to open and work with. This action is enabled when the repository contains submodules.
Creates a new stash from the changed files in the working copy.
Opens a dialog box that lists the existing stashes and lets you apply or remove a stash.
Opens a dialog box where you can add, edit, or delete existing remote repositories.
Opens a dialog box where you can select the remote branch that the local branch tracks for fetch, push, and pull commands.
Opens the repository configuration file in the main editor.
Opens a submenu with settings-related actions, such as opening the Git Client preferences page or resetting stored credentials.
